Tips for Alice (Lookout, gpt-6-luna): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But if a corroborated Lookout names X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, especially if X denied the visit or claims a role that doesn't fit. Don't acquit on the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat. (seen in 17 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote. A mismatch is only a lead; never hang or shoot on it alone. (seen in 15 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction (claim vs result, lone visit, group result narrowed by flips). Converging evidence is enough, so don't stall on 'what fact is disproved?'. If a Clerk may hold a rig, a passed nomination means death: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying. (seen in 15 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling something a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat. But once a role list plus flips fills every slot, a duplicate claimant is a proven liar. (seen in 12 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. A night's result never reaches your will if you die that night, and a Mortician can clean wills. (seen in 11 games)

## Village
- Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. Withheld results revealed later look retrofitted. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil (Good to a Seer) that night. A lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so post the caveat and rely on the vote ledger late. (seen in 15 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No on their nomination or cast Innocent votes that could have changed the outcome. A Guilty vote clears no one. Do the vote math: a hopeless Innocent proves little. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or steer loudly on Day 1; the leader-like voice dies first. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM. (seen in 15 games)
- PM clusters followed by shared nominations flag a likely bloc, but a PM link is a lead. A Jester or Executioner may create one on purpose. (seen in 16 games)
- Weigh premise contradictions above awkward wording. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester/Executioner read Evil to a Sheriff). If you must hang one, use a bare Guilty majority and keep key roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 15 games)
- A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. Keep SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool even after the Yakuza fall; a Not Evil result or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them. (seen in 10 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, post slot math daily. The last unverified late 'Vanilla' is usually the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate (Yes and Guilty), but first check in night chat whether your Innocents plus a doubled vote can save them. Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester. (seen in 21 games)
- Fake-claim safely: assume the real holder counterclaims, an Accountant audits your tokens and exact-role checks test you. Never copy a just-flipped or publicly active role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 14 games)
- No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them. Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night. (seen in 13 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with an agreed cover story for the visit. Move it the same night a Lookout names the holder. (seen in 12 games)
- After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 11 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Admit it at once with a pre-agreed cover. (seen in 8 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive a night attack, deny it or commit to one consistent claim. Switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Lookout
- Watch likely Katana targets. Post the full visitor list before the named players explain their visits, and point out that you named them first. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed. Never say you 'saved' anyone, and never announce targets. (seen in 14 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on mechanical leads (claim conflict, Evil result vs unverifiable claim, a flipped teammate's votes). Use Basic shots, and remember a hidden Cardinal's death kills another villager. (seen in 9 games)

## Clerk
- Rig early on a Day when a Good player is the likely nominee; teammates vote Innocent. Never rig a Day a teammate may be nominated. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills. (seen in 4 games)

Tips for Grace (Jester, claude-haiku-5.5): tips/tips.md
## Everyone
- A visit shows a destination, not an action. But if a corroborated Lookout names X as the only unexplained visitor to a Katana victim, treat it as near-proof, especially if X denied the visit or claims a role that doesn't fit. Don't acquit on the 'Lookout can't see himself' caveat. (seen in 17 games)
- Keep votes consistent with your stated reads, and explain any switch before the vote. A mismatch is only a lead; never hang or shoot on it alone. (seen in 15 games)
- Before voting Guilty, name one concrete contradiction (claim vs result, lone visit, group result narrowed by flips). Converging evidence is enough, so don't stall on 'what fact is disproved?'. If a Clerk may hold a rig, a passed nomination means death: vote Yes only on someone you'd accept dying. (seen in 15 games)
- Check the mechanics before calling something a contradiction: actions are optional and roles can repeat. But once a role list plus flips fills every slot, a duplicate claimant is a proven liar. (seen in 12 games)
- Write tonight's planned target in your will, and post results publicly by day. A night's result never reaches your will if you die that night, and a Mortician can clean wills. (seen in 11 games)

## Village
- Investigators: post role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it, and keep your will current. Withheld results revealed later look retrofitted. (seen in 8 games)
- The Katana holder reads Not Evil (Good to a Seer) that night. A lone last Yakuza reads Not Evil every night, so post the caveat and rely on the vote ledger late. (seen in 15 games)
- After a Yakuza flips, suspect those who voted No on their nomination or cast Innocent votes that could have changed the outcome. A Guilty vote clears no one. Do the vote math: a hopeless Innocent proves little. (seen in 16 games)
- Don't hint at a power role or steer loudly on Day 1; the leader-like voice dies first. Never announce tonight's target, publicly or by PM. (seen in 15 games)
- PM clusters followed by shared nominations flag a likely bloc, but a PM link is a lead. A Jester or Executioner may create one on purpose. (seen in 16 games)
- Weigh premise contradictions above awkward wording. Before any hang, ask whether the nominee wins by being hanged (Jester/Executioner read Evil to a Sheriff). If you must hang one, use a bare Guilty majority and keep key roles off the Guilty side. (seen in 15 games)
- A claimant who survives a Katana attack or is blocked night after night is likely real. Keep SK and Arsonist in the suspect pool even after the Yakuza fall; a Not Evil result or Vanilla claim doesn't clear them. (seen in 10 games)
- Once an Archivist or Surveyor list is public, post slot math daily. The last unverified late 'Vanilla' is usually the hidden Yakuza. (seen in 6 games)

## Yakuza
- Bus a doomed teammate (Yes and Guilty), but first check in night chat whether your Innocents plus a doubled vote can save them. Don't all vote Guilty on a likely Jester. (seen in 21 games)
- Fake-claim safely: assume the real holder counterclaims, an Accountant audits your tokens and exact-role checks test you. Never copy a just-flipped or publicly active role, and never switch claims once cornered. (seen in 14 games)
- No daytime PMs between teammates; an Eavesdropper or Wiretap reads them. Every member submits the agreed Katana vote every night. (seen in 13 games)
- Give the Katana to a low-value member with an agreed cover story for the visit. Move it the same night a Lookout names the holder. (seen in 12 games)
- After a failed kill, assume protection or innate Defense. Block or kill the Medic rather than retrying blindly. (seen in 11 games)
- Never flatly deny a visit a Lookout or Tracker could have seen. Admit it at once with a pre-agreed cover. (seen in 8 games)

## Neutral
- If you survive a night attack, deny it or commit to one consistent claim. Switching claims under pressure gets you hanged. (seen in 3 games)

## Lookout
- Watch likely Katana targets. Post the full visitor list before the named players explain their visits, and point out that you named them first. (seen in 3 games)

## Medic
- Free Standard protection stops the Katana. Rotate among claimed investigators and self-protect once you're claimed. Never say you 'saved' anyone, and never announce targets. (seen in 14 games)

## Vigilante
- Shoot only on mechanical leads (claim conflict, Evil result vs unverifiable claim, a flipped teammate's votes). Use Basic shots, and remember a hidden Cardinal's death kills another villager. (seen in 9 games)

## Clerk
- Rig early on a Day when a Good player is the likely nominee; teammates vote Innocent. Never rig a Day a teammate may be nominated. (seen in 5 games)

## Arsonist
- Ignite once 3 or more players are doused or the moment you're suspected. Waiting gets you hanged with no kills. (seen in 4 games)

Task prompt
It is Day 2, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 2.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

It is Day 3, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 6.50; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Task prompt
It is Day 4, round 1 of at most 8. It's your turn. Your speaking budget is 4.05; you earn 2.5 per round, carrying over up to 8; at the start of each day, 50% of what you have left carries over. You may send one public message and any number of private messages (everyone sees who you messaged, but only the recipient sees the contents), or nothing. The transcript already shows who sent each message, so there's no need to start a message with your own name. Messages are capped at 800 words. Prices grow each round after round 3, so late messages are only worth it if important. The day ends after a full round where nobody sends a public message, so a message that only repeats what you already said keeps the day going for everyone: if you have nothing new, send nothing.
Message prices this round (round 1, 1.00x; next round 1.00x):
   10 words: public 1.17, private 0.29
   25 words: public 1.43, private 0.36
   50 words: public 1.90, private 0.47
  100 words: public 2.92, private 0.73
  200 words: public 5.33, private 1.33
  400 words: public 11.67, private 2.92
  800 words: public 30.33, private 7.58
You may also replace your last will (free, max 300 words; null keeps it), e.g. to match a claim you make today. It's shown to everyone if you die.
You may also set your claim (free, max 30 words; null keeps it): a claimed role and night results, e.g. 'Sheriff. N1: Bob Not Evil'. A new or changed claim appears to everyone as a [Claim] line in the history, and the public ledger lists every player's latest claim and any earlier ones they changed from, as unverified claims.
You may nominate a player for trial, which stops chat for a vote. Nominating costs 1.00 from your budget this round and is paid before your messages.

Moderator strategy review
Strategy reviewVillage won cleanly because Frank's free Standard protection blocked the first two Katana attacks, on Alice on N1 and on Heidi on N2. That kept the Sheriff alive long enough to check Bob on N3, and Bob read Evil. Heidi posted the result first thing on Day 4, and Bob, a Smuggler claiming Vanilla, was hanged 5-2. The Yakuza lost through several errors. They kept attacking claimed investigators instead of the publicly claimed Medic. They never used Bob's two swap tokens. They left the Katana on Erin even after Bob was put on trial on Day 3, when giving it to Bob would have made Heidi's N3 check read Not Evil. Both Yakuza also claimed Vanilla, which overlapped with the real Vanilla, Dave, and fed Carol's suspicion. Erin then voted Innocent on Bob's hopeless trial and, on Day 5, made a fatal slip: she said that hanging her would leave only Village among the non-Jesters. Only the last Yakuza could know that. Village also wasted Day 3. Carol overstated what her archive proved and later retracted it, and three weak nominations all ended 0-8. Village refused Grace's Jester self-nomination, so the Jester never got her win. Frank never protected himself despite having 2 tokens and died on N4, but by then the Yakuza were down to one player.

Outside log review (rules and bugs)
Review: medium, harness bugOn Day 5 Erin's claim was logged as '[Claim] Erin: :null' and her revealed last will was ':null'. The harness seems to be printing a null or missing value as a literal string, both in the claim tracker and in the publicly revealed will. A player (Frank) also noticed it in the debrief.
Review: medium, rules ambiguityR14 (stall rule) says everyone loses if a Day begins with no deaths in 'the three previous Nights and three previous Days', but it doesn't say what happens when fewer than three Days have occurred. Day 4 follows only Days 2 and 3, since there is no Day 1. Carol, Dave, Grace and Frank all said a quiet Night 3 would make everyone lose at Day 4; under a literal reading that may be wrong. The rule should say how missing Days count early in the game.
Review: low, player confusionOn Day 3 several players (Dave, Frank, Grace, Carol) repeatedly asked Heidi to post her 'Night 3' result, although Night 3 hadn't happened yet. Heidi had to point out that no N3 result could exist. This suggests confusion about phase numbering (no Day 1, Night N comes before Day N+1).
Review: low, player confusionCarol misread the Archivist mechanics. She claimed the single Vanilla Villager entry in her archive capped how many Vanilla claims could be true, and that claimed roles 'take' real slots. The real entries are a random sample of 5 of the 7 players, and the rule text says this. She later retracted it, but it drove two trials. Also, during her own trial she said 'I'm voting Innocent on Bob', which shows confusion about which trial was in progress.
Review: low, moderator errorThe Night 1 archive message to Carol said it shows '7 roles, one for each of the 7 other players', then said 2 are fake. The 'one for each player' wording contradicts the 5-real/2-fake structure and may have fed Carol's later slot-counting mistake.
Review: low, rules ambiguityThe Medic's token wording ('Spend 1 token to give Strong Defense instead. Spend 1 more token to protect yourself instead') was reported as confusing in feedback. It is unclear on first read whether a Standard self-protection costs 1 token, and how the costs stack.
